# TLS-Anvil expected failures, keyed <TestClass>.<TestMethod>. Regenerated by
# tests/tlsanvil/run.sh --update-baseline; document every change in git.
#
# Snapshot 2026-09-14 (TLS-Anvil 1.5.x image of 2026-06-29, -strength 1,
# tls_blocking_server with the P-256 certificate): 152/199 passed, 47 failed
# (37 PARTIALLY_FAILED, 10 FULLY_FAILED), 200 disabled for features we do
# not offer (TLS 1.0/1.1, SSL 3, DTLS, PSK-only, RSA key exchange, CBC,
# client tests). The previous run (2026-05-07, older image) enabled 87 tests
# and passed 55. Families, with their disposition:
#
#  A. INTENTIONAL (RFC 8422 5.3): every TLS 1.2 test loses the parameter
#     combinations where the client lists ECDH_X25519 but not SECP256R1 in
#     supported_groups. "If the client has used a Supported Elliptic Curves
#     Extension, the public key in the server's certificate MUST respect the
#     client's choice of elliptic curves", so with a P-256 certificate we
#     answer handshake_failure; TLS-Anvil expects a ServerHello. Covers the
#     PARTIALLY_FAILED entries of ClientHello.*, ClientInitiatedExtensionPoints.*,
#     DoNotUseSSLVersion30.*, E1Compatibility*, FfDheShare.*, Fragmentation.*,
#     HappyFlow.*, PaddingExtension.serverDoesNotEcho, PointFormatExtension.*,
#     RespectClientExtensions.*, ServerHello.*, ServerKeyExchange.*,
#     SignatureAlgorithms.{includeUnknown*,offerManyAlgorithms}, SupportedVersions.*,
#     TLSExtensionForECC.*, CertificateStatusRequest.* and the X25519 half of
#     SignatureAlgorithms.ecdsaNoSignatureAlgorithmsExtension.
#  B. INTENTIONAL (RFC 9155): SignatureAlgorithms.ecdsaNoSignatureAlgorithmsExtension
#     expects SHA-1 when the client sends no signature_algorithms extension
#     (RFC 5246 7.4.1.4.1 default); we sign with SHA-256. Same call as the
#     tlsfuzzer chacha20 "Chacha20 in TLS1.1" exclusion.
#  C. TO FIX -- lenient length-field parsing (both versions): a ClientHello
#     extension whose declared length overruns or underruns its body, an
#     inner list length that disagrees with the body (psk_key_exchange_modes,
#     supported_versions, pre_shared_key identities too short), stray bytes
#     after the last extension, and renegotiation_info with a wrong length
#     are all accepted; RFC 8446 6.2 wants decode_error. TLS 1.3 variants
#     answer HelloRetryRequest because the walker stops before key_share.
#     Entries: *ExtensionLength*, *ListLength*, PreSharedKeyExtension.*,
#     SupportedVersionsExtension.*. Needs a strict extension walker and
#     per-extension inner-length checks, with proofs; own PR.
#  D. TO FIX -- plaintext records after the handshake: a plaintext
#     ChangeCipherSpec is ignored on both versions (RFC 8446 5 / RFC 5246 7.1
#     want unexpected_message), and an undefined record type gets a
#     close_notify on TLS 1.2 instead of unexpected_message. Entries:
#     StateMachine.secondChangeCipherSpec*, TLSRecordProtocol.sendNotDefinedRecordTypes*.
#  E. TO TRIAGE: AlertProtocol.closeNotify ("expected 1 warning alert, got 2";
#     the same exchange with OpenSSL and Python clients shows exactly one
#     close_notify each way and a closed socket).
